title: Outlook: custom organisation properties on profile cards
summary: Hold: the connection-creation call misleadingly places contentCategory under configuration, although Microsoft documents it as a property of the connection itself. The rollout, default and Message Center admin path are supported, but the checklist also asserts a hiding behaviour that the risk section explicitly says is not documented for these custom properties.

claims.quote: These properties can be sourced from external systems like HR platforms, enriching user profiles with relevant organizational details.

claims.claim: No API for the connector-sourced property display settings is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "connector" "profile cards" "custom" "API" "visibility". Opened: customize-profile-cards, peopleconnectors, build-connectors-with-people-data, add-properties-profilecard, Create profileCardProperty. claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The people-connector starting point is Connectors gallery > Human resources & recruiting in the Microsoft 365 admin center, not a fully documented navigation sequence.
claims.quote: Browse the Connectors gallery in the Microsoft 365 admin center and check the Human resources & recruiting category.

claims.claim: Create a people connection with POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections (configuration contentCategory = people).
claims.quote: configuration ... Specifies additional application IDs that are allowed to manage the connection and to index content in the connection. Optional. ... contentCategory ... Possible values are: ... people
claims.fix: Replace the call with 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections (contentCategory = people)' and explicitly say contentCategory is a top-level externalConnection property, not inside configuration. Keep the existing POST reference and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/externalconnectors-externalconnection for the property location. The configuration resource at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/externalconnectors-configuration documents only authorizedAppIds.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The checklist treats hiding connector custom properties as having a known effect on other experiences, while the risk section says that effect is undocumented.
claims.quote: Whether the same holds for connector custom properties is not documented. ... Validate the values with HR before ingesting them, because hiding a property on cards does not stop it appearing in other Microsoft 365 experiences.
claims.fix: Replace the At rollout bullet with 'Validate the values with HR before ingesting them: connector people data is visible to all users by default and is used by other Microsoft 365 experiences. Do not rely on card visibility as a data boundary.' This uses the documented ingestion and data-usage facts without asserting an undocumented effect of the new hiding control.

claims.fix: Add a controls row 'Tenant-wide switch for connector-sourced custom properties', scope tenant, ui null and api null, with a note distinguishing the missing whole-feature switch from the per-property visibility documented in MC1193692.
